simple: GPU code that gives the right answer whatever the number of lanes in a warp or wavefront.
analogy: a recipe card that says "the first helper of each row counts" instead of "the helper at seat 0, 32, 64… counts".
precise: code that takes the lock-step group width from warpSize (or a host query of the device's warpSize property), stores lane masks in 64 bits, elects leaders with threadIdx.x % warpSize, and keeps width-dependent tuning values in per-target tables; in HIP 5.7 warpSize is a per-target compile-time constant (64 for gfx90a, 32 for gfx1030 in this build's assembly).
source: C1 (Systems Curriculum 13.1: "never hard-code 32 in portable code"), H2 and R12 of BR-02 (pending verification; dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a library you can swap in by renaming calls, without changing what the program means.
analogy: the second kitchen building's own spice mix: maybe the same, maybe not; you taste before you serve.
precise: a claim, checked per function and per version, that a library on one platform offers the same functions, arguments, data layouts, status codes and results as one on another; a renaming translator cannot establish it (in BR-02's run the teaching translator left every cuBLAS call in place and reported nothing untranslated).
source: D8 of BR-02 (library documentation, title only) and R17 of BR-02 (pending verification; dossier gate G1 open)
